title: projectStateRevision contract (G0 freeze)
initialValue: 1, set once by the migration baseline. The baseline writes exactly one migration_baseline event; it never fabricates a historical transaction sequence and never reuses any legacy counter.

increments.record_only: Advances exactly once per committed record_only outcome (Review terminal + Receipt are canonical review history; no research object is touched).
increments.create_decision: Advances exactly once per committed decision creation or transition.
increments.add_evidence: Advances exactly once per committed evidence creation, state change, provenance change, or link change.
increments.create_or_resolve_issue: Advances exactly once per committed issue creation, status transition, or resolution.
increments.patch_brief: Advances exactly once per committed Brief patch producing a new active version.
increments.formal_direction_change: Advances exactly once per committed direction change producing a new Brief version with supersession marker.
increments.record_only_outcome: Advances exactly once; the outcome transaction is the same transaction as its Receipt and revision event, never a second advance.
increments.memory_governance_change: Advances once per committed Memory confirm, edit, stale, expire, renew, retire, forget, or privacy redaction (project-governed context changed).
increments.compensation: Advances N to N+1; a rollback or compensation never decreases the revision and never resurrects an old Manifest, even if the canonical hash returns to an old value.
increments.migration_baseline: Sets revision 1 with one baseline event; no further advance for the baseline itself.

optimisticConcurrency: A commit compares the expected projectStateRevision with the current head inside the write transaction. The head is advanced by compare-and-swap; any mismatch fails the transaction with a stale-revision conflict. A stale preview is never silently rebased and never auto-committed; the user rebuilds the preview and re-confirms.
conflictBehavior: On a revision conflict: the transaction rolls back, the Review keeps its persistent pre-commit state, and the system reports the exact changed objects and revisions. Two Reviews prepared on the same revision may both exist; only the first commit wins and the second becomes stale.
failureRevisionBehavior: Any failure inside the commit transaction leaves the revision unchanged. There is no intermediate observable revision: the head, the event, the resulting object, the Review terminal state, and the Receipt either all land or none do. A commit whose outcome is unknown after a crash is resolved by authorityCommandId lookup, never by guessing.

receiptTraceBinding.receipt: Every transition Receipt records beforeProjectStateRevision and afterProjectStateRevision and references the revision event id.
receiptTraceBinding.trace: Every revision event records projectId, revision, transactionId, effectKind, reviewId (when applicable), changedObjectRefs, previousCanonicalHash, nextCanonicalHash, publicSummary, and createdAt.
receiptTraceBinding.recoveryRule: Recovery validates the head against the append-only event chain; a broken chain fails closed and blocks writes.

derivedProjectionRule: Search, Attention, Today, Resume, and History projections carry their source projectStateRevision. A stale projection is displayed as rebuilding; it never becomes a write source and never impersonates the current revision.
recoveryRule: After any restore or crash recovery, the runtime reloads the head and validates the event chain before any write. A mismatch enters Recovery with writes locked; the revision is never rewound.
